name: Tony Visconti
hook: An American who moved to London to produce records and ended up following David Bowie to a studio 150 metres from the Berlin Wall.

blurb.age7: Tony Visconti produced many of David Bowie's albums over several decades, including ones made in Berlin.
blurb.age13: Visconti moved from Brooklyn to London in the late 1960s and began a decades-long, on-and-off production partnership with David Bowie. He produced 'Young Americans' (1975) and then, alongside Brian Eno, two of the three Berlin Trilogy albums recorded at Hansa Studios: 'Low' and '"Heroes"' (both 1977).
blurb.adult: Visconti's collaboration with Bowie spans decades and styles, from the 'plastic soul' of 'Young Americans' to the Eno-assisted Berlin records, making him one of this dataset's clearest examples of a producer whose relationship with one artist outlasted any single genre both of them passed through.

signatureTracks.title: Young Americans (produced for David Bowie)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The 'plastic soul' record, and evidence Visconti and Bowie's partnership predates the Berlin period most associated with it.

signatureTracks.title: "Heroes" (produced for David Bowie)
signatureTracks.whyThisOne: Co-produced with Brian Eno at Hansa Studios, about 150 metres from the Berlin Wall.
